title: What a council is
hookLine: bishops from across the whole Church gather, with the pope, to settle a question too big for one person

lines: A WAITING ROOM, LATE AT NIGHT.
cards: A hospital waiting room, late at night. A family has a hard question in front of it: how to care for a parent who can't live alone anymore. Everyone has a view.
Someone talks too long; someone goes quiet. And at some point, if it goes well, they land on something they can all stand behind, and they say it out loud, together.

The Church has done this too, on questions at the heart of its faith, with bishops in the room instead of brothers and sisters. A new stretch of the year starts today, with a word: ecumenical council.

teach.b: The pattern starts in the Bible.

In the Acts of the Apostles, the first followers of Jesus hit a question that could have split them: when people who weren't Jewish came to believe, did they need to be circumcised and keep the law of Moses?
The text says, "And the apostles and ancients assembled to consider of this matter." A long debate followed. Peter spoke.
Paul and Barnabas told what they had seen God do. James proposed a way forward.

teach.h: IT HATH SEEMED GOOD TO THE HOLY GHOST AND TO US.
teach.b: And the letter they sent out carries a remarkable phrase: "For it hath seemed good to the Holy Ghost and to us." Not us alone. The Holy Ghost, and us.
Some readers call that gathering in Jerusalem the first council. Later, when the Church had spread far beyond Jerusalem, it met the same way, only larger.

teach.h: BISHOPS FROM EVERYWHERE, WITH THE POPE.
teach.b: An ecumenical council is a gathering of bishops from across the whole Church, together with the pope, to settle a question of faith or life for everyone.

The Catechism says the college of bishops exercises its authority over the whole Church in a solemn way in such a council, and that no council is ecumenical unless Peter's successor confirms it, or at least accepts it as such.
Catholics believe the Holy Spirit guards what the bishops, with the pope, teach together as definitive on faith and morals. Orthodox Christians honor the early councils too.
Over the coming weeks, this path walks through several councils, each beginning with a question too big for one person.

how: Catholics receive the teaching of the ecumenical councils as binding on the whole Church; the Nicene Creed said at Sunday Mass grew from the early councils.

games.why: the apostles and ancients assembled, heard Peter, Paul, Barnabas and James, and wrote: it hath seemed good to the Holy Ghost and to us.

practice: Bring to mind a time you decided something with others, a family, a team, a parish council, and look not at the outcome but at the room: who spoke, who listened, what it took to come to one mind.
If it went badly, notice that too without replaying the argument, and ask what the group leaned on besides its own cleverness. If you pray, give thanks for the people at that table with you.
